passage:
In class ten, Jatin told everyone that Jomon was the best friend anyone could have. Jomon lent pens, waited after class and never forgot a birthday. Then Jomon arrived late to Jatin's cricket match. By evening Jatin was calling Jomon a fake and telling others not to trust anyone who behaves like that. There was no room in his mind for a friend who could be warm and forgetful together.
At twenty, Jatin was picked to lead a group project. The first week he did everything himself: slides, survey and the report, and he was worn out by Friday. The second week he swung the other way and sent each person a piece with a message saying "done by the deadline". Nobody heard from him again. Parveen vanished, one member grumbled at the workload, and two parts did not fit together.
At last he made a shared sheet with one name against each piece, and set a single check-in on Wednesday at four. Parveen turned up with a finished section. Jomon, now in the same group, brought tea.

qa.q: On which day and at what time did Jatin set the single check-in?
qa.a: He set it on Wednesday at four.

qa.q: What thinking style shows up in both Jatin's view of Jomon and his way of leading the group?
qa.a: Jatin swings between everything and nothing. He called Jomon the best friend anyone could have, then a fake; as leader he did everything himself, then sent each person a piece and vanished, until a shared sheet with one name against each piece and a single check-in gave a middle path.

qa.q: What was Jatin probably feeling when Jomon arrived late to the cricket match?
qa.a: He was hurt and let down, and that strong feeling made it hard to see Jomon's good sides beside the lateness.

qa.q: What could Jatin try next if a group member misses the Wednesday check-in?
qa.a: He could ask them calmly what is blocking them, and adjust the piece or offer help while keeping the same owner and deadline.

grounding: All-good-then-all-bad thinking about a friend (3896) echoes an all-or-nothing way of sharing group tasks (5046), fixed by clear owners and one checkpoint.
